content.text: Our clang-format system has erroneously replaced ">>>" with "> > >" in our CUDA files where we try to launch CUDA kernels. What is the way to prevent clang-format from doing this?
I’ll check the repository’s formatting guidance and the relevant clang-format option so the recommendation matches your setup.

content.text:
Set the project’s clang-format language standard to C++11 or newer:

```yaml
Standard: Cpp11
```

Your root [`.clang-format`](/Users/mfrancis/Documents/gkeyll/code/gkeyll_v0/gkeyll/.clang-format:119) currently has `Standard: Cpp03`. Under C++03, clang-format treats adjacent closing angle brackets as needing separation, producing `> > >`; with `Cpp11`, CUDA launches remain:

```cpp
kernel<<<blocks, threads>>>(...);
```

Beyond changing the configured standard or disabling formatting around the line, the only practical alternative is to exempt CUDA files/directories from clang-format in your formatting script or pre-commit hook.

There is no CUDA-specific clang-format knob for this. CUDA is formatted using the C++ parser, and `Cpp03` is what causes `>>>` to be split. Excluding `.cu` files works, but means losing automatic formatting for all CUDA code, so I would avoid it.
